51377288.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Keap1 Kelch domain (321 to 609 residues) (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: Isothermal titration calorimetry experiments were carried out on a MicroCal ITC-200 system (GE Healthcare) using Keap1 protein (Kelch domain = aa321–aa609) that had been passed through a PD-10 column (GE Healthcare) equilibrated with 10 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% (v/v) Tween 20, 1 mM TCEP, pH 7.40, and 1% DMSO. Complete titration of 60 μM Keap1 was typically achieved by injecting 19 × 2 μL aliquots of a 0.6 mM compound at a temperature of 25 °C and a spacing interval of 90 s between injections. The thermodynamic binding parameters were extracted by nonlinear regression analysis of the binding isotherms (Microcal Origin version 7.0 software package). A single site binding model was applied, yielding binding enthalpy (ΔH), stoichiometry (n), entropy (ΔS), and association constant (K_a).
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption - ITC data: Determination of the dissociation constant (K_D) for the binding of 14 to Keap1 by isothermal titration calorimetry. The raw heat signals from the exothermic binding reaction (left) have been integrated to yield a binding isotherm (right) from which the thermodynamic parameters were extracted (insert). The dissociation constant was obtained from three measurements on three distinct samples and is reported as the mean value ± standard deviation.
original_paragraph.Figure 2c - ITC thermogram and binding i: The left panel shows the raw heat signals (DP in μcal/sec) over time (min) for the titration. The right panel shows the integrated binding isotherm, plotting the binding enthalpy (kcal/mol of injectant) against the molar ratio of ligand to protein. The fitted curve yields a K_D of 3.7 ± 0.8 μM. The insert shows the thermodynamic parameters: ΔG = -10.0 kcal/mol, ΔH = -12.0 kcal/mol, and TΔS = +2.0 kcal/mol.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 10 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% (v/v) Tween 20, 1 mM TCEP, 1% DMSO
